sentences.text: It is the petitioner's case that acquisition of part of the subject land has lapsed by virtue of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner refers to the counter affidavit filed by the Land Acquisition Collector (LAC) and has drawn the attention of this Court to paragraph 7 of the said affidavit wherein it is stated that the possession of the part of the subject land was not taken and compensation has not been paid.
sentences._hearing_file: Harish Gupta vs Union Of India And Ors on 15 May, 2024.json

sentences.text: However, the learned counsels appearing for the respondents submit that notwithstanding the fact that possession of the subject land has not been taken and compensation has not been paid, the acquisition has not lapsed as the same was for Rohini Residential Scheme and in terms of the order dated 10.03.2015 of the Supreme Court in Rahul Gupta v. Delhi Development Authority & Ors.:SLP(C) No.16385-88/2012, the possession is deemed to have been taken over.

sentences.text: He submits that by a subsequent order dated 28.01.2016, the Court had noted that in that case the physical possession of the subject land was available with DDA for carving into plots for allotment to various allotees.

sentences.text: 2. He submits that it is in the said context that the Court had held that it was not possible to accept the legitimacy of the continued possession of the applicants in that case.
